- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- After a price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike height to avoid overshoot.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment (≥0.8) followed by low sentiment, model often fails to revert; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; apply linear decay adjustment: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day from day 5 onward.
- If sentiment history shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment up but price down), model often misreads sentiment; use sentiment as a lagged momentum filter: if sentiment > 0.7 and price falls, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
